name: Two by two
intent: Trade two axes off against each other and place items.
when: prioritising or comparing under two competing values
prompt: Place each option in a quadrant. Nothing may sit on a line.
readback: Name what landed in each quadrant and challenge the crowding — a quadrant holding everything is an axis that isn't discriminating.

claims.claim: Placing items on a spatial layout defined by two explicit dimensions makes their relative standing on both dimensions easier to judge and compare than a list or table does.
Items placed inside the same bounded region are perceived as belonging together, even against other grouping cues, so labelled zones make category membership readable at a glance.
claims.construct: the Gestalt principle of common region (perceptual grouping)

grounding.helps: when items need comparing on two values at once; laying them on two axes is diagram craft with no direct test, so treat the quadrants as a prompt to argue with, not a measurement
grounding.backfires: when an axis does not discriminate and everything crowds one quadrant, or when "nothing on a line" forces a false either-or; neither risk has been studied, and in classroom studies the gains from graphic organisers did not carry over to later tasks
